## Conclusion

Transformer architectures remain one of the most powerful and versatile patterns in modern AI. From language to vision to multimodal systems, these models are the backbone of 2026’s intelligent applications. Whether you’re experimenting with small models or designing large‑scale workflows, understanding the structure and practical implementation of Transformers is essential. [...] ·

Feb 8, 2026

Transformer models have become one of the most important innovations in AI over the past decade. First introduced in 2017 in the paper “Attention Is All You Need”, Transformers power many of the systems we use today — from language models like GPT and Claude to vision systems, multimodal agents, and more. As of 2026, Transformer architectures remain the core building block for modern AI, but they have evolved in power, scale, efficiency, and application. [...] This simple pipeline allows Transformers to excel at many tasks.

## 3. Real‑World Transformer Variants in 2026

As of today, several Transformer variants are widely used:

## 3.1 Language Transformers

 GPT (OpenAI) — generative language model
 LLaMA / LLaMA2 / LLaMA3 (Meta) — open and research‑focused language models
 Claude (Anthropic) — AI assistant optimized for safety

These variants differ in training data, scale, safety layers, and usage licenses.

# Industrial Time Series Forecasting with Transformer Networks

Transformer architectures have become the dominant paradigm for predictive analytics in manufacturing, energy, and IIoT. This landscape maps 70+ retrieved records spanning 2020–2026 across key technical clusters, leading assignees, and emerging filing directions.

patent and literature records in this dataset

Explore in Eureka [...] Salesforce's 2026 US patent on a mixture-of-experts transformer routes heterogeneous time series patterns to specialized feed-forward expert layers via a gating function, predicting output distributions rather than scalar values. This architecture generalizes across heterogeneous time series types and represents a shift from task-specific to general-purpose industrial forecasting foundation models, analogous to what GPT did for language according to the report.
